answer: A registry can resist fake identities by rate-limiting sign-ups: each new agent identity must wait through a growing queue before it can transact, like a trellis that only lets one vine through at a time. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents faces a thousand waiting periods, while a genuine newcomer passes a quill-smooth onboarding check. A velvet rope of small, escalating registration fees per identity from the same controller makes bulk creation expensive without pricing out honest single agents.
